subject: Harmonizing transfer safeguards: SCC mapping, UK Addendum decisions, and escrow path
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ellie Park <ellie.park@globexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Harmonizing transfer safeguards: SCC mapping, UK Addendum decisions, and escrow path

Hi team / Ellie,

Quick primer and ask: Globex has signaled they want a single harmonized approach for EU-to-UK and EU-to-US flows for their pilot. They asked whether SCCs + our standard UK Addendum (IDTA) is sufficient, or if a bespoke TIA/DTIA + escrow for logs is required.

What I need from us this week:
- Kimberly: a short mapping (SCCs clauses -> our operational controls) and a callout of any gaps that would push us to require a TIA.
- Laura: legal decision matrix on when we require escrow/escrow-like custody for logs vs when an onshore cache / fallback is acceptable.
- Marissa: proposed customer-facing timeline and the minimal evidence bundle Globex needs to sign (so Sales can commit).

Ellie, to set expectations on Globex side: can you confirm whether they require physical custody/escrow for audit logs, or if an access-controlled remote escrow (with DFARS-style dual control) would be acceptable? Also, target go/no-go date for the pilot is end of September.

I attached a first-pass mapping sheet (SCCs_mapping_v3.xlsx) and a draft TIA scope (TIA_scope_draft.docx) for context.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SCCs_mapping_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), TIA_scope_draft.docx (docx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellie Park <ellie.park@globexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Harmonizing transfer safeguards: SCC mapping, UK Addendum decisions, and escrow path

Connor — thanks for the context. I reviewed the mapping you shared and annotated a few operational gaps. High-level notes:

1) SCCs mapping: most standard SCC obligations (encryption-in-transit, role-based access, subprocessors notice, incident timelines) are covered by our current controls and instrumentation (see sheet).
2) UK Addendum / IDTA: the addendum handles the legal mechanism for UK recipients; operationally we need to confirm egress logging and retention alignment with their retention policy (Globex wants 12 months).
3) Gaps that push to a TIA: anything involving customer-managed keys, or a requirement for segregated physical escrow of logs.

Recommendation: aim for SCCs + UK Addendum as default. If Globex insists on "custodial escrow" for logs (i.e., third-party sealed storage with controlled release), escalate to legal + procurement and plan for a TIA. Otherwise we can mitigate with: onshore cache + signed attestation from our infra team + retained audit snapshots for 12 months.

I can produce a 1-page technical attestation and a redline in the mapping sheet by EOD tomorrow.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Harmonizing transfer safeguards: SCC mapping, UK Addendum decisions, and escrow path

Hi Connor / Kimberly / team,

Thanks for the quick turn. To clarify Globex's position: they are open to SCCs + UK Addendum for most processing, but given the sensitivity of audit logs for the pilot (pseudonymized patient flows), their compliance team prefers a custody model for logs unless we can provide a contractual attestation + technical isolation that meets their audit requirements.

Their asks for the decision:
- A clear statement whether Redwood can provide a signed technical attestation that logs will be retained for 12 months and protected under the stated controls.
- If not, confirmation of the estimated timeline/cost for an escrow/TIA path.

Pilot timing is flexible but they would like a firm commitment on the transfer approach by 2026-09-15 to keep vendor signoffs moving.

Ellie Park
Head of Data Privacy Ops
Globex Health

Ellie Park

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ellie Park <ellie.park@globexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Harmonizing transfer safeguards: SCC mapping, UK Addendum decisions, and escrow path

Thanks — summary and decision log below.

Summary of decisions (internal):
- Default approach: SCCs + UK Addendum (IDTA) plus a signed technical attestation covering retention and access controls. This meets legal and most operational obligations for the pilot.
- Escrow / TIA triggers: require TIA if customer mandates third-party physical escrow of logs, customer-managed keys, or additional custodial release controls. We will not pursue escrow by default (cost and procurement timeline).
- Evidence bundle for Globex: 1) signed Technical Attestation (to be produced by Kimberly), 2) SCCs mapping XLSX (Connor will deliver redline), 3) UK Addendum decision memo (I will draft and circulate for approvals).

Next steps / owners and timeline:
- Kimberly: Technical Attestation draft (due 2026-09-10 COB).
- Connor: Annotated SCCs mapping v3 (due 2026-09-10 COB).
- Laura: Draft UK_Addendum_decision_memo (circulate for Legal + Privacy review by 2026-09-11).
- Marissa: Customer-facing milestone doc and proposed signature timeline (send to Ellie by 2026-09-11).

Ellie — if Globex accepts the attestation path, we will avoid the TIA/escrow procurement and can commit to the pilot timelines. Please confirm acceptance by 2026-09-12 so we can lock internal approvals.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

Attachments: UK_Addendum_decision_memo.pdf (placeholder to be drafted)
